prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the large seated or reclining person directly in front of the camera wearer throughout frames 1–3, roughly 0.3–0.8 m away, while the raised feet/hands and surrounding room surfaces are generally farther away, about 1–3 m; brighter protruding limbs are the nearest parts. In frame 4, two hands holding objects appear within roughly 0.3–0.6 m of the camera, with a person’s head and upper body farther ahead near the center-right at about 0.8–1.5 m; in frame 5, the head at lower right and adjacent forearm are extremely close, probably 0.2–0.5 m, while another person at the upper right is around 1–2 m away. Across the strip, the viewpoint turns from the nearby torso toward the right-hand side of the room, bringing the close head and arm into view while the earlier body moves left and out of frame. The map makes near/far layering, limb protrusion, and occlusion boundaries clearer than the dark RGB, but its metric distances are only rough: large uniform regions, haloed edges, and the saturated white lower-right foreground in frame 5 indicate unreliable depth around close bodies and occlusions.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation identifies a cat low on the left in frame 1 and several people: one large person occupying most of frames 1–3, plus multiple partly visible people in frame 5; these masks separate overlapping bodies that merge together in the dark RGB. The cat is left of and below the nearby person, apparently about 0.5–1.5 m from the camera wearer and close to the person’s left side, while the dominant person’s torso is directly ahead within roughly 0.3–0.8 m; frame 5 shows one very close person at lower right and another farther person at upper right, separated by roughly 0.5–1.5 m. The changing masks show the camera turning right: the dominant foreground person expands across frames 2–3, disappears in frame 4, and re-enters partly at the right edge in frame 5, where several people are heavily cropped or mutually occluded. The map is unreliable in frames 2–3, where an oversized person mask absorbs background and possibly multiple surfaces, and in frame 5, where one body is split into differently colored regions and small holes or fragments appear.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates nearby hands that are difficult to distinguish against the dark RGB: one hand lies upper-left in frame 1, another near the upper middle in frame 2, another near center in frame 3, two hands appear center-right in frame 4, and a pair of hand detections lies near the upper-right in frame 5. Their locations indicate that hands repeatedly enter the camera wearer’s immediate forward workspace, approximately 0.2–0.7 m away and generally within arm’s reach; in frame 4 the two hands are close to one another, likely separated by about 0.2–0.4 m, while the frame-5 detections are vertically separated near the same person. The sequence shows the hand region shifting from left to center to right as the viewpoint turns, with some hands rotating or changing foreshortening rather than showing a clear approach or retreat. No dependable body skeleton, head orientation, gaze direction, or facing direction is recovered, so the map cannot establish whether anyone looks toward the camera wearer; it is also unreliable because limbs and torsos are almost entirely missing and some magenta contours may trace objects or partial hands rather than complete hand poses.
